## Load data

```{r}
#| message: false
patients  <- read_tsv(here("data", "01_patients.tsv"))
samples   <- read_tsv(here("data", "01_samples.tsv"))
mutations <- read_tsv(here("data", "01_mutations.tsv"))
```


## Cleaning mutations to keep variables of interest

Selecting variables of interest

```{r}
mutations_clean <- mutations |> 
                      select(c("Tumor_Sample_Barcode",
                               "Hugo_Symbol", 
                               "Chromosome", 
                               "Start_Position", 
                               "End_Position", 
                               "Strand", 
                               "Consequence",
                               "Variant_Type",
                               "Mutation_Status"))
```

Splitting the Tumor_Sample_Barcode into a Patient_id matching the one in the other 2 tables and a Tumor_Barcode

```{r}
mutations_clean <- mutations_clean |> 
                      mutate(patient_id = str_sub(Tumor_Sample_Barcode, 
                                                  start = 1, 
                                                  end = 9)) |> 
                      mutate(Tumor_Sample_Barcode = str_sub(Tumor_Sample_Barcode, 
                                                            start = 11)) |> 
                      rename(tumor_barcode = Tumor_Sample_Barcode) |> 
                      relocate(patient_id) |> 
                      rename(hugo_symbol = Hugo_Symbol,
                             chromosome = Chromosome,
                             start_position = Start_Position,
                             end_position = End_Position,
                             strand = Strand,
                             consequence = Consequence,
                             variant_type = Variant_Type,
                             mutation_status = Mutation_Status) |> 
                      select(-strand) 
```

## Cleaning patients data set

Renaming Patient_id to match mutations column and modifying the way status is logged in the table.

```{r}
patients_clean <- patients |> 
                      rename(patient_id = PATIENT_ID,
                             sex = SEX,
                             os_months = OS_MONTHS,
                             os_status = OS_STATUS,
                             age_group =  AGE_GROUP,
                             drug_type = DRUG_TYPE) |> 
                     mutate(status = str_sub(os_status, 
                                      start = 3),
                             .keep = "unused")
```

```{r}
patients_clean <- patients_clean |> 
                    mutate(age_group = factor(age_group,
                                              levels = c("<30",
                                                        "31-50",
                                                        "50-60",
                                                        "61-70",
                                                        ">71")))
```
### Compairing patients list to mutations 

Selecting one patient (chosen randomly)

```{r}
patients |> 
  filter(PATIENT_ID == "P-0024731")
```

Looking at all the tumors linked to this patient in the mutations data set.

```{r}
mutations |> 
  filter(str_detect(Tumor_Sample_Barcode,"P-0024731"))

```

```{r}
patient_id <- 
  patients|> 
    select(PATIENT_ID) |> 
    rename(id = PATIENT_ID)
```

```{r}
dim(patient_id)
dim(tumor_id)
```

Since there are more patients than tumor samples, we need to identify which patients do not have tumors, in order to eliminate them from the data set we want to work with in the end.

### Extracting a list of patient ID from the mutations data set to subset samples and patients

```{r}
tumor_patient <- mutations_clean |> 
                    group_by(patient_id) |> 
                    count() |> 
                    rename(number_mutations = n)
```

Extracting rows corresponding to patients present in the mutations table and adding to patients_clean a column with number of mutations.

```{r}
patients_clean <- patients_clean |> 
                      inner_join(tumor_patient, join_by("patient_id"))
```

## Cleaning the samples data set

Selecting variables of interest

```{r}
samples_clean <- samples |> 
                    select(c("PATIENT_ID", 
                             "SAMPLE_ID",
                             "CANCER_TYPE",
                             "SAMPLE_TYPE",
                             "METASTATIC_SITE",
                             "PRIMARY_SITE",
                             "CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED",
                             "SOMATIC_STATUS")) |> 
                    rename(patient_id = PATIENT_ID) |>                       
                    mutate(sample_barcode = str_sub(SAMPLE_ID, 
                                      start = 11),
                             .keep = "unused")
                    
```

Extracting rows corresponding to patients present in the mutations table.

```{r}
samples_clean <- samples_clean |>
                    rename(cancer_type = CANCER_TYPE,
                           sample_type = SAMPLE_TYPE,
                           metastatic_site = METASTATIC_SITE,
                           primary_site = PRIMARY_SITE,
                           cancer_type_detailed = CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED,
                           somatic_status = SOMATIC_STATUS) |> 
                    semi_join(tumor_patient, by = "patient_id")
```

Joint tables patients and samples table

```{r}
cancer_clean <- patients_clean |> 
                      inner_join(samples_clean, join_by("patient_id"))
```

## Save clean data and tidy the environment

Rename the two tables for the next steps, save them, and remove everything
else from the environment, so that it's not too cluttered

```{r}
clinical <- cancer_clean
mutations <- mutations_clean

save(clinical,
     mutations,
     file = here("data", "02_cancer_clean.RData"))

rm(list = setdiff(ls(),
                  c("clinical",
                    "mutations")))
```
